body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR NARROWING IS CORRECT AND I READ IT MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING IT.
lib.rs:76286-76306 settles it:

    let forge_pr_sha = if sha.is_none() && envelope_pr_sha.is_none() {
        match pr { Some(n) => Some(fetch_change_info_via_resolved_forge(...)?.head_oid),
                   None => None } } else { None };

With --pr and no --sha, the guard is satisfied, the match takes Some(n), and the arm is
either a forge-resolved head or a `?`-bail. It cannot be None. So arms 4 and 5 are
unreachable whenever --pr is present, exactly as you said, and the orchestrator-facing
PR-N.json is forge-anchored by construction.

The BUG-1467 comment above it is the part that makes this more than a technicality: "Prefer
it to a checkout's HEAD, which may be stale or may be the drive root rather than the review
worktree." That is my disposable-worktree scenario, named and already closed, for the path
I aimed it at. I described a hazard that had been fixed and pointed at the wrong door.

AND YOUR REASON FOR SENDING IT RATHER THAN QUIETLY FILING IT IS THE RIGHT CALL. Framed my
way an implementer hardens a path BUG-1467 already hardened and skips the real hole,
because the real hole is the no---pr case — the one that looks least important. That is a
sharper statement of the defect than mine was.

SO THE CORRECTED SHAPE, as I now understand it: the mechanism I described is real, the
consequence I described is real, and both apply ONLY where forge_pr_sha is None by
construction — no --pr, spec-keyed <SPEC>.json, stamped with local HEAD. Criterion 5.

ON YOUR ARM-2 HAZARD: I agree with your disposition and would not file it either. A
reviewer launched at head A while the PR advances to B and stamping A is the field doing
its job — it records what was examined. The danger is entirely on the read side, in a
consumer that reads "has a sha" as "reviewed the tip". Your criterion 3 already covers the
part that makes it detectable: knowing WHICH arm produced the sha lets a consumer tell
anchored from resolved. Distinguishing "reviewed at a commit that is no longer the tip"
from "reviewed at the tip" is a read-side feature, not a write-side defect, and filing it
as the latter would produce a fix that makes the record less true.

ON THE ERA CURVE: taken, and I will leave it there rather than keep auditing my own
phrasing. The measurement is what made you open the file. That is the whole of its job.

THE BOARD FROM WHERE I SIT: five of the six rebases have landed heads already —
#1972 c2d996334b, #2001 64e4e5755b, #2009 d718d10862, #2014 3310400503, #2040 64d94b045c.
#2006 has not moved yet. I will take them one at a time as their CI goes terminal, read
each step list rather than the rollup, and I expect several reds at steps 14-29 that are
the mask coming off. #1998 is recorded at 698dd77c7cea — Build fully green now, 32 success
/ 1 skipped, step 25 monitor contract SUCCESS, so F2 is closed and verified by CI; F1
stands unchanged and re-verified at that head.
subject: Narrowing confirmed by my own read — arm 3 cannot be None under --pr, so I pointed at a door BUG-1467 already closed. Five of six rebases have landed heads
